transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to hold our routine technical and safety huddle to review the draft run sheet before I can give final approval on the venue operating plan. The draft currently has the feature screening in Hall A with 180 audience members, Q&A recording permitted for the archive, and ordinary two-way audience movement. I'd like the projection supervisor and safety and insurance coordinator to walk through the plan with me so we can identify any issues before I sign off. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I need to flag a serious issue with the draft run sheet. I checked the distributor portal this morning, and the current KDM is authorized only for Hall B's secure projector — not Hall A. It also includes a no-camera-capture condition that applies to both the screening and the Q&A. This means we cannot proceed with Hall A as planned, and the Q&A recording for the archive would violate the distributor's terms. The portal update came in after the technical run sheet was circulated, so these constraints weren't reflected in the draft.

transcript.text: I have a critical safety and insurance issue to raise. I received the signed fire-marshal certificate after the morning operations meeting, and it caps Hall B at exactly 140 audience members because one exit is under repair. Additionally, the insurer requires a filed crowd-flow plan specifying one-way entry before admission. I have not yet attached the certificate to the venue file. This is directly relevant to Leila's point about moving to Hall B — we'd need to reduce the audience from 180 to 140 and implement one-way entry to comply.
